newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZOG to spud another Chevril well in June.
newsitem.headline: NZOG to spud another Chevril well in June.

text.p: New Zealand Oil and Gas said on Thursday a new oil well about to be drifted off the west coast of Western Australia was expected to add to the life and profitability of the productive Airlie oil fields.
The Chervil-6 infill/appraisal well is expected to spud on or about June 23, NZOG said in a statement.
"The Chervil well is being drilled to determine the thickness of the existing oil column which currently produces 450 barrels of oil per day.

"If this well establishes that sufficient quantities of oil have moved to the top of the reservoir, a horizontal well will be drilled to maximise the drainage rate and ultimate recovery of the remaining oil."
NZOG said good productivity rates were possible, as shown by the current two wells in the Chervil field which produced at initial combined rates of 4,000 barrels per day.

"A successful Chervil-56 well could lead to a three to four fold increase in the rate of production from Chervil," NZOG said. About 3.4 million barrels of oil had been recovered from the two producing wells in Chervil since 1989.
